app.name: PureMail
app.description: Modern email with thread-linked tasks, follow-ups, and right-pane work tracking.

tools.name: getMailContext
tools.description: Return the selected account, the query the mail list is currently showing, its result count, and the selected thread. Includes workspaceFolder, the absolute path of the user's workspace; saveAttachments and saveMessageAsPdf write into its Mail folder.

tools.name: listThreads
tools.description: List mail threads matching a query. Query syntax is the same string the user types in the search box: in:inbox from:x subject:y label:"z" is:unread|read|starred|snoozed|important|other|triaged|untriaged triage:needs_reply|important|fyi|noise has:attachment|calendar before:/after:YYYY-MM-DD older_than:30d newer_than:7d sort:newest|oldest|sender|subject limit:N, and any operator may be negated with a leading '-'. Returns the canonical query, the total match count, and the threads.

query.description: Query string. Empty means every thread in the account inside the fetch window, excluding Trash.

tools.name: searchAllMail
tools.description: Search ALL of the user’s mail on the server — not limited to the locally synced window. Works on Gmail (Gmail search syntax verbatim: from:, before:, older_than:, has:attachment …) and on IMAP accounts such as Proton Mail via Bridge (plain-text search across every folder). On Gmail, out-of-window results can be imported with getThread; on IMAP they cannot — relay their details directly.

query.description: Gmail search syntax, sent to Gmail verbatim.

tools.name: getThread
tools.description: Read one thread: its subject, participants, labels, status and messages. Each message lists its attachments with their name, type (PDF, Doc, Sheet, Slides, Text, Image…), size and whether it is a document — saveAttachments saves them as files.

includeBodies.description: Include full message bodies rather than snippets.

tools.name: showQuery
tools.description: Point the user's mail list at this query so they can read exactly what you are working with. Use before applying a bulk action so the user sees the affected set.

tools.name: listViews
tools.description: List the user's saved named queries.

tools.name: saveView
tools.description: Save a query as a named view pinned in the user's sidebar. Saving an existing name replaces its query.

tools.name: deleteView
tools.description: Delete one of the user’s saved views by name.

tools.name: applyMailAction
tools.description: Apply a bulk action over the threads matching a query, immediately: archive, trash, read, unread, label, snooze, move, star, or unstar. The affected query is shown in the user's list and the change is recorded in the mail log. Destructive actions (trash) only at the user's direction.

snoozedUntil.description: ISO timestamp; required when action is 'snooze'.

rationale.description: One line explaining why, shown to the user.

mailboxName.description: Required when action is "move": the mailbox name or id to move the threads to.

tools.name: markThreadsRead
tools.description: Mark specific threads read or unread by id. applyMailAction covers a whole query; this names threads. Applied immediately, synced to the account in the background, and recorded in the mail log. Threads already in the requested state are left alone and listed as alreadyThere.

threadIds.description: Thread ids from listThreads, searchAllMail or getThread.

read.description: false marks the threads unread; true marks them read.

tools.name: nextTriageBatch
tools.description: The next untriaged threads to judge, packed to fit one tool result. Each row carries the latest message cleaned of quoted history and signatures (text; cut when shortened) and facts the app knows for certain: who sent last (last), message count, unread, cc when the user is only on Cc, draft when an unsent draft exists, file names, a calendar invite, bulk when the sender marks it as bulk mail, before when a new message reopened a thread already triaged, and sender history (replied: messages the user has sent them; marked: the verdict the user last gave this sender themselves). The app makes no judgment: you decide every verdict. Judge the whole batch, call recordTriage once with every id and its at, then call again until remaining is 0. Use getThread only when an excerpt is not enough to decide. Do not page through listThreads or listDrafts to triage.

scope.description: Which mail to triage, in the search syntax listThreads uses. Default in:inbox newer_than:1d. Narrow it with newer_than:2d or a label; untriaged is added for you.

limit.description: Most threads in one batch (default and maximum 12). A batch also ends when the next thread would not fit.

tools.name: recordTriage
tools.description: Record your verdict on every thread of a batch, in one call. Verdicts: needs_reply (they are waiting on an answer or a decision from the user), important (no reply owed, but the user should know or act: deadlines, money, changes, people who matter), fyi (worth a glance), noise (safe to ignore). Each decision needs the id and at from nextTriageBatch, a verdict and a one-line reason; give an action for needs_reply and important, the concrete next step. A thread whose at no longer matches got a new message: it comes back as stale, is not recorded, and returns in the next batch. Recording marks the threads triaged in the app, where the user sees the verdict and can change it. Nothing is sent or changed in the mailbox.

decisions.description: One decision per thread in the batch.

at.description: The at nextTriageBatch gave for this thread.

action.description: The concrete next step, for needs_reply and important.

scope.description: The scope you are triaging, so remaining counts the right mail. Default in:inbox.

tools.name: getTriageReport
tools.description: The triage decisions recorded since a time: needs_reply first, then important, then fyi, and noise only when asked; newest first within each. Each item has the thread id, subject, from, reason, action, when it was decided, by: you when the user set it themselves, done when the user has replied since, and reopened when a new message came in and the thread is back in the triage queue. counts covers every verdict in the window. Build reports from this instead of re-reading mail. When nextOffset is present, call again with it for the rest.

since.description: An ISO date or a span back from now: 12h, 1d (default), 1w.

include.description: Which verdicts to list. Default needs_reply, important, fyi.

offset.description: Where to continue: the nextOffset from the previous call.

tools.name: listMailChanges
tools.description: The mail log: recent mail changes from the operations ledger, newest first, with actor lane, kind, and summary. Check it before repeating work another agent already did.

tools.name: draftReply
tools.description: Prepare reply context only. Returns requestId, account/thread identity, voice, reply intent and source text. Write the reply yourself in this drawer, then call commitReplyDraft(requestId, body). This tool creates no draft and starts no internal agent.

threadId.description: Thread to draft a reply to. Defaults to the thread the user has open.

instructions.description: Optional brief for a fresh draft, or the change to make to the existing draft (e.g. "shorter, confirm Tuesday").

tools.name: commitReplyDraft
tools.description: Apply a drawer-written reply to a prepared request. Rejects expired, reused or stale source/draft requests. Reuses the existing unsent generated draft; never sends. Read back with getDraft. Applied is not proof of disk persistence or provider sync.

tools.name: composeMessage
tools.description: Compose a NEW outgoing message (its own thread in Drafts), not a reply to an existing thread. Use draftReply to answer a conversation. Pass `attachments` (absolute file paths) to attach documents in the same call — they are read and checked against the 25 MB sending limit before the draft is made, so a refused file leaves nothing behind. Drafts never send themselves.

to.description: Recipients, comma-separated. Accepts "Name <email>" or a bare address.

body.description: The message text you have written for the user to review.

attachments.description: Optional absolute paths of files to attach (e.g. /Users/developer/Pure/Reports/q3.pdf). Relative paths are refused.

tools.name: listDrafts
tools.description: List drafts, newest first — every unsent draft wherever it was written, including ones that failed to generate. Read this back after drafting rather than assuming a draft exists.

includeSent.description: Include drafts that have already been sent. Defaults to false.

tools.name: getDraft
tools.description: Read one draft in full, including its body, by draftId.

draftId.description: The draft to read. Ids come from draftReply, composeMessage or listDrafts.

tools.name: updateDraft
tools.description: Rewrite an existing unsent draft. Read getDraft first and provide its version as expectedVersion to reject concurrent edits.

expectedVersion.description: Exact version returned by getDraft. Required to prevent overwriting concurrent edits.

tools.name: discardDraft
tools.description: Delete an unsent draft, here and at the provider. Irreversible — only when the user asked for it.

tools.name: addDraftAttachments
tools.description: Attach local files to an unsent draft by ABSOLUTE path (e.g. /Users/developer/Pure/Reports/q3.pdf). Call listDrafts or getDraft first for the draftId — the draft must already exist (commitReplyDraft/composeMessage create one; a compose window the user has not saved is not a draft yet). Reads the bytes the same way the compose window's Attach button does and appends them; the attachments total must stay under the 25 MB sending limit or the whole call is refused and nothing is attached. A file already on the draft (same name and size) is skipped, not added twice. Attachments are sent only when the user sends the draft.

draftId.description: The draft to attach to. Ids come from draftReply, composeMessage or listDrafts.

paths.description: Absolute file paths to attach, in order. Relative paths are refused.

tools.name: removeDraftAttachment
tools.description: Remove one attachment from an unsent draft. Prefer attachmentId (from getDraft or addDraftAttachments); name works only when exactly one attachment has that name. Returns the attachments that remain.

attachmentId.description: The attachment's id, as getDraft lists it.

name.description: Fallback: the attachment's file name. Refused when two attachments share it.

tools.name: saveAttachments
tools.description: Save a thread's attachments as files into the Mail folder of the user's workspace and return each file's absolute path — how documents (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, XML…) get out of mail. Call getThread first to see the attachments. By default only documents are saved (images are skipped and listed); pass `names` to pick files, or only: "all". A file forwarded down the thread is saved once, from the newest message. Attachments not yet downloaded are fetched from the mail server. Files are written as new files: nothing is overwritten (a clash gets " (1)" added). There is no choice of folder.

threadId.description: The thread whose attachments to save. Ids come from listThreads, searchAllMail or getThread.

messageId.description: Optional: only this message's attachments. getThread lists message ids.

names.description: Optional: the attachments to save, by name (as getThread lists them). Named files are saved whatever their type.

tools.name: saveMessageAsPdf
tools.description: Save an email as a PDF document in the Mail folder of the user's workspace: the whole thread (oldest message first) or one message, with each message's From, To, Cc, date and subject, its body as the reader shows it (remote images left out) and a list of its attachments. The attachments themselves are not inside the PDF — use saveAttachments for those. The file is named after the subject and never overwrites a file already there. Returns the PDF's absolute path. There is no choice of folder.

threadId.description: The thread to save. Ids come from listThreads, searchAllMail or getThread.

messageId.description: Optional: save only this message rather than the whole thread.

tools.name: createMailTask
tools.description: Create a task linked to a mail thread.

tools.name: listFilters
tools.description: List the user's mail filters with their queries, actions, and hit counts.

tools.name: createFilter
tools.description: Create a mail filter: a named query (same language as search) with actions. Applies to newly synced threads; nothing retroactive happens without applyFilterRetroactively.

name.description: Short filter name shown in settings.

query.description: Match query, e.g. from:news@example.com or from:example.com.

labelName.description: Label to apply; created if missing.

fileIntoBox.description: Also skip the inbox and pin the label's view as a sidebar box.

tools.name: applyFilterRetroactively
tools.description: Run one existing filter over the user's existing threads. Confirm with the user before calling — this archives/labels real mail.

tools.name: createBox
tools.description: Create a sidebar box: a label plus its pinned view. Use createFilter with fileIntoBox to keep filing mail into it.

tools.name: deleteFilter
tools.description: Delete a filter rule by name or id. Threads it already filed stay where they are.

tools.name: setFilterEnabled
tools.description: Pause or resume a filter rule by name or id without deleting it.

tools.name: listBoxes
tools.description: List the boxes (folders) with thread counts. account_folder entries are real folders on the mail server (IMAP accounts); local_box entries are label-backed views on this device. A filed thread lives in its box, out of the inbox and out of Archive.

tools.name: fileThread
tools.description: File one thread into a box without creating a rule. If the box names a real account folder (IMAP accounts — see listBoxes), the thread MOVES to that folder on the mail server. Otherwise the box label is applied locally and the thread archives on the provider.

tools.name: openThread
tools.description: Open one thread in the user’s reader. Ask the user in chat FIRST — this moves their screen. For several results, prefer showQuery.

tools.name: listRuns
tools.description: List send runs (mail-merge sessions reviewed one draft at a time): id, name, status (setup | ready | running | paused | done), progress, template and recipient summary. Archived runs are hidden unless includeArchived. Call getRun before acting on one.

tools.name: getRun
tools.description: Read one run in full: status, cursor, every item with its status (pending | reviewing | sent | skipped | missing), draft id, recipient and note flag; the field map and available {{tokens}}; recipient validation (invalid and duplicate rows with reasons); the template's subject, body and tokens. Call this FIRST before renderRun, setRunNote, sendRunItem or skipRunItem — ids and rows come from here.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: createRun
tools.description: Start a send run in setup: a template draft (an existing unsent draft by id, or a new one — optionally seeded with subject/body) plus, optionally, the recipient list right away (recipients: pasted addresses one per line as `email`, `Name <email>` or `email, name`; or recipientsPath: an ABSOLUTE .csv or .sheets path). Template conventions: {{field}} tokens substitute per recipient from the mapped columns ({{first_name}}, {{email}}, or any column name); ONE {{note}} slot marks the personal line typed per draft — dropped entirely from drafts where it is left empty. Write or revise the template afterwards with updateDraft(templateDraftId, { subject, body }) in plain text. Nothing sends here; renderRun creates the drafts and the user (or sendRunItem, one per approved call) sends them.

name.description: A short run name ("October workshop invite").

templateDraftId.description: An existing unsent draft to use as the template. Omit to create a fresh template draft.

body.description: Template body as plain text; {{tokens}} and one {{note}} allowed.

recipientsPath.description: Absolute path to a CSV file or a PureSheets .sheets package (first sheet, header row).

fieldMap.description: token → column, e.g. {"email":"Email","first_name":{"column":"Name","transform":"first-word"}}. Guessed from column names when omitted.

tools.name: createRunFromDrafts
tools.description: Inherit existing unsent drafts into a run (no template, no list): the loop then reviews and sends them one at a time, in the order given. The drafts stay ordinary drafts — editable in Drafts and in the run. Use listDrafts for the ids. Nothing sends here.

draftIds.description: Unsent draft ids, in review order.

tools.name: renderRun
tools.description: Render (or re-render) the run's drafts from its template: one ordinary draft per valid recipient row, {{tokens}} substituted, the template's attachments on each, the {{note}} slot left empty for the loop. Idempotent: unsent drafts update in place (a note already typed is kept), sent items are never touched, rows that dropped out lose their unsent draft. Invalid addresses and duplicates are excluded with reasons. Requires a template with content and a mapped email column — getRun shows both. Nothing sends.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: setRunNote
tools.description: Write the personal note into one item's {{note}} slot ("add a personal line for Mere"). Plain text; replaces any note already there. Refused when the draft has no slot — then edit its body with updateDraft, or insert a slot in the template and renderRun again. The draft stays unsent.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

draftId.description: The item's draft id (as getRun lists it). Omit both draftId and row to mean the item the run is currently on.

row.description: The item's 1-based recipient row (as getRun lists it). Alternative to draftId.

tools.name: sendRunItem
tools.description: Send ONE run item — the current one, or the one named by draftId/row — through the normal send path: the draft as it stands now (an empty {{note}} slot is stripped), the usual undo hold, Sent as normal. Marks the item sent and moves the run to the next open item. There is deliberately no send-all: call this once per item, and each call is approved by the user separately. Never call it in a loop without the user asking for each send.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

draftId.description: The item's draft id (as getRun lists it). Omit both draftId and row to mean the item the run is currently on.

row.description: The item's 1-based recipient row (as getRun lists it). Alternative to draftId.

tools.name: skipRunItem
tools.description: Skip one run item (the current one, or by draftId/row) without sending: its draft stays in Drafts and the run moves on. A skipped item can still be sent later by revisiting it.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

draftId.description: The item's draft id (as getRun lists it). Omit both draftId and row to mean the item the run is currently on.

row.description: The item's 1-based recipient row (as getRun lists it). Alternative to draftId.

tools.name: pauseRun
tools.description: Pause a run. It keeps its place and resumes there later — even after the app is closed.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: resumeRun
tools.description: Continue a paused or ready run at its first open item and put it on the user's screen (this moves their view — say so). Returns the current item; from there the user presses Send & next per draft, or sendRunItem sends one per approved call.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: setRunRecipients
tools.description: Attach or replace a run's recipient list: recipients (pasted, one per line: `email`, `Name <email>`, or `email, name`) or recipientsPath (an ABSOLUTE .csv path, or a PureSheets .sheets package — first sheet, header row). The field map is guessed from the column names (email, first name / first word of a name, full name) unless fieldMap is given; check it in the result and fix it with setRunFieldMap. Returns validation: valid rows, invalid rows with reasons, duplicates. If the run already has rendered drafts, renderRun again afterwards.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

fieldMap.description: token → column, e.g. {"email":"Email","first_name":{"column":"Name","transform":"first-word"},"role":"Role"}. Column names must match the list's columns exactly (getRun lists them).

tools.name: setRunFieldMap
tools.description: Map template tokens to list columns for a run: which column is the email (required to render), which is the first name (add transform "first-word" to take the first word of a full name), and any other token the template uses. Merges into the existing map. getRun shows columns, the current map and availableTokens.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

fieldMap.description: token → column, e.g. {"email":"Email","first_name":{"column":"Name","transform":"first-word"},"role":"Role"}. Column names must match the list's columns exactly (getRun lists them).

tools.name: setRunTemplate
tools.description: Point a run at its template: an existing unsent draft by draftId, or (with no draftId) the run's current template — created if it has none — optionally writing subject and/or body (plain text). Template conventions: {{field}} tokens substitute per recipient from the mapped columns; exactly one {{note}} slot marks the personal line typed per draft, dropped from drafts where it is left empty. Keep editing the template with updateDraft(templateDraftId, { subject, body }).

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

draftId.description: An existing unsent draft to use as the template.

tools.name: insertRunNoteSlot
tools.description: Add a {{note}} slot to the run's template if it has none — after the first paragraph by default, or at the end. The slot is where the personal line goes during the run; it is dropped from drafts where it stays empty. No-op when the template already has one.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: previewRunItem
tools.description: Render ONE recipient row from the template without creating anything: the To, subject and body exactly as renderRun would write them, plus any tokens the list cannot fill. Defaults to the first valid row. Use it to check a template before renderRun.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: addDraftsToRun
tools.description: Append existing unsent drafts to a run's loop (the "Add existing drafts…" door): they are reviewed and sent one at a time like rendered items, and stay ordinary drafts. Drafts already in the run are skipped; listDrafts shows ids.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.

tools.name: archiveRun
tools.description: Archive a DONE run: it leaves the Runs rail; the record and its sent mail stay. Refused while the run still has open items — pauseRun or skipRunItem those first.

runId.description: The run's id, from listRuns or getMailContext.activeRuns.
